field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PoC, fuzz input, or regression test was executed; the finding is static.

NVD scores the issue 7.5 with AV:N, but the reported crash requires a cJSON array whose internal prev link is NULL. The public JSON parser does not build that shape; reachability therefore depends on application code that constructs or corrupts arrays through the API. This caveat is not reflected in the NVD vector.

The independent reviewer found that the maintainer could not reproduce the reporter's stated trigger in issue #802, and that the reporter's mechanism description is imprecise: line 2279 overwrites newitem->prev before line 2287 reads it, so the L2287 dereference requires after_inserted->prev to be NULL (a corrupted array), while the newitem == NULL case fails earlier at line 2278.

NVD CPE lists only 1.7.16, while the same unguarded code exists in earlier releases and Debian records introduced 0. The canonical affected_range follows the upstream fix boundary (<1.7.17) and keeps the NVD scope narrower.
The first fix commit 60ff122 contained a wrong check (newitem->prev instead of after_inserted->prev); release 1.7.17 only becomes correct with follow-up f66cbab.
The same fix commit also carries the separate CVE-2023-50472 change in cJSON_SetValuestring; this dossier does not evaluate that CVE.

critical_operation.description: cJSON_InsertItemInArray() only rejects which < 0. It copies after_inserted->prev into newitem->prev and then, for a non-first element, dereferences newitem->prev at line 2287. If the array element's prev link is NULL (a corrupted or manually assembled list), that dereference is a NULL-pointer write. The v1.7.17 fix adds `newitem == NULL` at function entry and rejects `after_inserted != array->child && after_inserted->prev == NULL`; the first attempt in 60ff122 tested the not-yet-assigned newitem->prev and was corrected by f66cbab.

entry_point.description: The exported API cJSON_InsertItemInArray(cJSON *array, int which, cJSON *newitem) declared in cJSON.h is the entry point. Any application that mutates a cJSON array and calls this function with a NULL newitem, or with an array whose element has a NULL prev link, reaches the unguarded dereference. The parser (cJSON_Parse) does not itself create that link shape; this is an API-level reachability constraint, not a claim of remote exploitability.

Whether applications commonly pass an unchecked NULL newitem to this API was not surveyed.
Debian's 12 fix (1.7.15-1+deb12u1) was not compared line by line with the upstream fix.
